segs.e: Numbered Discourses 1.1–10
The Chapter on What Occupies the Mind
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekarūpampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, itthirūpaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single sight that occupies a man’s mind like the sight of a woman.

segs.p: Itthirūpaṁ, bhikkhave, purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.
segs.e: The sight of a woman occupies a man’s mind.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekasaddampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, itthisaddo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single sound that occupies a man’s mind like the sound of a woman.

segs.p: Itthisaddo, bhikkhave, purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.
segs.e: The sound of a woman occupies a man’s mind.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekagandhampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, itthigandho.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single smell that occupies a man’s mind like the smell of a woman.

segs.p: Itthigandho, bhikkhave, purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.
segs.e: The smell of a woman occupies a man’s mind.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekarasampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, itthiraso.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single taste that occupies a man’s mind like the taste of a woman.

segs.p: Itthiraso, bhikkhave, purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.
segs.e: The taste of a woman occupies a man’s mind.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekaphoṭṭhabbampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, itthiphoṭṭhabbo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single touch that occupies a man’s mind like the touch of a woman.

segs.p: Itthiphoṭṭhabbo, bhikkhave, purisassa cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.
segs.e: The touch of a woman occupies a man’s mind.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekarūpampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, purisarūpaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single sight that occupies a woman’s mind like the sight of a man.

segs.p: Purisarūpaṁ, bhikkhave, itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.
segs.e: The sight of a man occupies a woman’s mind.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekasaddampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, purisasaddo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single sound that occupies a woman’s mind like the sound of a man.

segs.p: Purisasaddo, bhikkhave, itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.
segs.e: The sound of a man occupies a woman’s mind.”

segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single smell that occupies a woman’s mind like the smell of a man.

segs.p: Purisagandho, bhikkhave, itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.
segs.e: The smell of a man occupies a woman’s mind.”

segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single taste that occupies a woman’s mind like the taste of a man.

segs.p: Purisaraso, bhikkhave, itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.
segs.e: The taste of a man occupies a woman’s mind.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekaphoṭṭhabbampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, purisaphoṭṭhabbo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single touch that occupies a woman’s mind like the touch of a man.

segs.p: Purisaphoṭṭhabbo, bhikkhave, itthiyā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī”ti.
segs.e: The touch of a man occupies a woman’s mind.”
Numbered Discourses 1.11–20
The Chapter on Giving Up the Hindrances

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppanno vā kāmacchando uppajjati uppanno vā kāmacchando bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, subhanimittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to sensual desire, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow like the feature of beauty.

segs.p: Subhanimittaṁ, bhikkhave, ayoniso manasi karoto anuppanno ceva kāmacchando uppajjati uppanno ca kāmacchando bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: When you apply the mind irrationally to the feature of beauty, sensual desire arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppanno vā byāpādo uppajjati uppanno vā byāpādo bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭighanimittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to ill will, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow like the feature of aversion.

segs.p: Paṭighanimittaṁ, bhikkhave, ayoniso manasi karoto anuppanno ceva byāpādo uppajjati uppanno ca byāpādo bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: When you apply the mind irrationally to the feature of aversion, ill will arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannaṁ vā thinamiddhaṁ uppajjati uppannaṁ vā thinamiddhaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, arati tandī vijambhitā bhattasammado cetaso ca līnattaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to dullness and drowsiness, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow like discontent, sloth, yawning, sleepiness after eating, and mental sluggishness.

segs.p: Līnacittassa, bhikkhave, anuppannañceva thinamiddhaṁ uppajjati uppannañca thinamiddhaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: When you have a sluggish mind, dullness and drowsiness arise, and once arisen they increase and grow.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannaṁ vā uddhaccakukkuccaṁ uppajjati uppannaṁ vā uddhaccakukkuccaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cetaso avūpasamo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to restlessness and remorse, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow like an unsettled mind.

segs.p: Avūpasantacittassa, bhikkhave, anuppannañceva uddhaccakukkuccaṁ uppajjati uppannañca uddhaccakukkuccaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: When your mind is unsettled, restlessness and remorse arise, and once arisen they increase and grow.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannā vā vicikicchā uppajjati uppannā vā vicikicchā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, ayonisomanasikāro.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to doubt, or, when it has arisen, makes it increase and grow like irrational application of mind.

segs.p: Ayoniso, bhikkhave, manasi karoto anuppannā ceva vicikicchā uppajjati uppannā ca vicikicchā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: When you apply the mind irrationally, doubt arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppanno vā kāmacchando nuppajjati uppanno vā kāmacchando pahīyati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, asubhanimittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents sensual desire from arising, or, when it has arisen, gives it up like the feature of ugliness.

segs.p: Asubhanimittaṁ, bhikkhave, yoniso manasi karoto anuppanno ceva kāmacchando nuppajjati uppanno ca kāmacchando pahīyatī”ti.
segs.e: When you apply the mind rationally to the feature of ugliness, sensual desire does not arise, or, if it has already arisen, it’s given up.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppanno vā byāpādo nuppajjati uppanno vā byāpādo pahīyati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, mettā cetovimutti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents ill will from arising, or, when it has arisen, gives it up like the heart’s release by love.

segs.p: Mettaṁ, bhikkhave, cetovimuttiṁ yoniso manasi karoto anuppanno ceva byāpādo nuppajjati uppanno ca byāpādo pahīyatī”ti.
segs.e: When you apply the mind rationally to the heart’s release by love, ill will does not arise, or, if it has already arisen, it’s given up.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannaṁ vā thinamiddhaṁ nuppajjati uppannaṁ vā thinamiddhaṁ pahīyati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, ārambhadhātu nikkamadhātu parakkamadhātu.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents dullness and drowsiness from arising, or, when they have arisen, gives them up like the elements of initiative, persistence, and vigor.

segs.p: Āraddhavīriyassa, bhikkhave, anuppannañceva thinamiddhaṁ nuppajjati uppannañca thinamiddhaṁ pahīyatī”ti.
segs.e: When you’re energetic, dullness and drowsiness do not arise, or, if they’ve already arisen, they’re given up.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannaṁ vā uddhaccakukkuccaṁ nuppajjati uppannaṁ vā uddhaccakukkuccaṁ pahīyati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cetaso vūpasamo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents restlessness and remorse from arising, or, when they have arisen, gives them up like a settled mind.

segs.p: Vūpasantacittassa, bhikkhave, anuppannañceva uddhaccakukkuccaṁ nuppajjati uppannañca uddhaccakukkuccaṁ pahīyatī”ti.
segs.e: When the mind is settled, restlessness and remorse do not arise, or, if they’ve already arisen, they’re given up.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannā vā vicikicchā nuppajjati uppannā vā vicikicchā pahīyati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, yonisomanasikāro.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that prevents doubt from arising, or, when it has arisen, gives it up like rational application of mind.

segs.p: Yoniso, bhikkhave, manasi karoto anuppannā ceva vicikicchā nuppajjati uppannā ca vicikicchā pahīyatī”ti.
segs.e: When you apply the mind rationally, doubt does not arise, or, if it’s already arisen, it’s given up.”
Numbered Discourses 1.21–30
The Chapter on the Unworkable

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ abhāvitaṁ akammaniyaṁ hoti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so unworkable as this mind that is not developed.
An undeveloped mind is unworkable.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ kammaniyaṁ hoti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so workable as this mind that is developed
A developed mind is workable.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ abhāvitaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not developed.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, abhāvitaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: An undeveloped mind is very harmful.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is developed.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, bhāvitaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: A developed mind is very beneficial.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ abhāvitaṁ apātubhūtaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not developed or manifested.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, abhāvitaṁ apātubhūtaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: An undeveloped and unmanifested mind is very harmful.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ pātubhūtaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is developed and manifested.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, bhāvitaṁ pātubhūtaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: A developed and manifested mind is very beneficial.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ abhāvitaṁ abahulīkataṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not developed and cultivated.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, abhāvitaṁ abahulīkataṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: An undeveloped and uncultivated mind is very harmful.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ bahulīkataṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is developed and cultivated.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, bhāvitaṁ bahulīkataṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: A developed and cultivated mind is very beneficial.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ abhāvitaṁ abahulīkataṁ dukkhādhivahaṁ hoti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that brings such suffering as this mind that is not developed and cultivated.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, abhāvitaṁ abahulīkataṁ dukkhādhivahaṁ hotī”ti.
segs.e: An undeveloped and uncultivated mind brings suffering.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ bahulīkataṁ sukhādhivahaṁ hoti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that brings such happiness as this mind that is developed and cultivated.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, bhāvitaṁ bahulīkataṁ sukhādhivahaṁ hotī”ti.
segs.e: A developed and cultivated mind brings happiness.”
Numbered Discourses 1.31–40
The Chapter on the Untamed

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ adantaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not tamed.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, adantaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: An untamed mind is very harmful.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ dantaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is tamed.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, dantaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: A tamed mind is very beneficial.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ aguttaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not guarded.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, aguttaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: An unguarded mind is very harmful.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ guttaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is guarded.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, guttaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: A guarded mind is very beneficial.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ arakkhitaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not protected.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, arakkhitaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: An unprotected mind is very harmful.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ rakkhitaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is protected.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, rakkhitaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: A protected mind is very beneficial.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ asaṁvutaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not restrained.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, asaṁvutaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: An unrestrained mind is very harmful.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ saṁvutaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is restrained.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, saṁvutaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: A restrained mind is very beneficial.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ adantaṁ aguttaṁ arakkhitaṁ asaṁvutaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very harmful as this mind that is not tamed, guarded, protected, and restrained.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, adantaṁ aguttaṁ arakkhitaṁ asaṁvutaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: An untamed, unguarded, unprotected, and unrestrained mind is very harmful.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ dantaṁ guttaṁ rakkhitaṁ saṁvutaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very beneficial as this mind that is tamed, guarded, protected, and restrained.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, dantaṁ guttaṁ rakkhitaṁ saṁvutaṁ mahato atthāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: A tamed, guarded, protected, and restrained mind is very beneficial.”
Numbered Discourses 1.41–50
The Chapter on a Spike

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sālisūkaṁ vā yavasūkaṁ vā micchāpaṇihitaṁ hatthena vā pādena vā akkantaṁ hatthaṁ vā pādaṁ vā bhecchati lohitaṁ vā uppādessatīti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, suppose a spike of rice or barley was pointing the wrong way. If you trod on it with hand or foot, it is impossible for it to break the skin and produce blood.
Why is that?
Because the spike is pointing the wrong way.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, so vata bhikkhu micchāpaṇihitena cittena avijjaṁ bhecchati, vijjaṁ uppādessati, nibbānaṁ sacchikarissatīti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: In the same way, it is quite impossible for a mendicant whose mind is pointing the wrong way to break ignorance, produce knowledge, and realize extinguishment.
Why is that?
Because their mind is pointing the wrong way.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sālisūkaṁ vā yavasūkaṁ vā sammāpaṇihitaṁ hatthena vā pādena vā akkantaṁ hatthaṁ vā pādaṁ vā bhecchati lohitaṁ vā uppādessatīti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, suppose a spike of rice or barley was pointing the right way. If you trod on it with hand or foot, it’s possible it may break the skin and produce blood.
Why is that?
Because the spike is pointing the right way.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, so vata bhikkhu sammāpaṇihitena cittena avijjaṁ bhecchati, vijjaṁ uppādessati, nibbānaṁ sacchikarissatīti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: In the same way, it is quite possible for a mendicant whose mind is pointing the right way to break ignorance, produce knowledge, and realize extinguishment.
Why is that?
Because the mind is pointing the right way.”

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, bhikkhave, ekaccaṁ puggalaṁ paduṭṭhacittaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: “Mendicants, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual whose mind is corrupted, I understand:

segs.p: ‘imamhi ce ayaṁ samaye puggalo kālaṁ kareyya, yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye’.
segs.e: ‘If this individual were to die right now, they would be placed in hell as if delivered there.’
Why is that?
Because their mind is corrupted.

segs.p: Cetopadosahetu pana, bhikkhave, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjantī”ti.
segs.e: Corruption of mind is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, bhikkhave, ekaccaṁ puggalaṁ pasannacittaṁ evaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi:
segs.e: “Mendicants, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual whose mind is pure, I understand:

segs.p: ‘imamhi ce ayaṁ samaye puggalo kālaṁ kareyya, yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge’.
segs.e: ‘If this individual were to die right now, they would be placed in heaven as if delivered there.’
Why is that?
Because their mind is pure.

segs.p: Cetopasādahetu pana, bhikkhave, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjantī”ti.
segs.e: Purity of mind is the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, udakarahado āvilo luḷito kalalībhūto tattha cakkhumā puriso tīre ṭhito na passeyya sippisambukampi sakkharakaṭhalampi macchagumbampi carantampi tiṭṭhantampi.
segs.e: “Suppose, mendicants, there was a lake that was cloudy, murky, and muddy. A person with clear eyes standing on the bank would not see the clams and mussels, pebbles and gravel, and schools of fish swimming about or staying still.
Why is that?
Because the water is clouded.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, so vata bhikkhu āvilena cittena attatthaṁ vā ñassati paratthaṁ vā ñassati ubhayatthaṁ vā ñassati uttariṁ vā manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṁ sacchikarissatīti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: In the same way, that a mendicant whose mind is clouded would know what’s for their own good, the good of another, or the good of both; or that they would realize any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones: this is quite impossible.
Why is that?
Because their mind is clouded.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, udakarahado accho vippasanno anāvilo tattha cakkhumā puriso tīre ṭhito passeyya sippisambukampi sakkharakaṭhalampi macchagumbampi carantampi tiṭṭhantampi.
segs.e: “Suppose, mendicants, there was a lake that was transparent, clear, and unclouded. A person with clear eyes standing on the bank would see the clams and mussels, pebbles and gravel, and schools of fish swimming about or staying still.
Why is that?
Because the water is unclouded.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, so vata bhikkhu anāvilena cittena attatthaṁ vā ñassati paratthaṁ vā ñassati ubhayatthaṁ vā ñassati uttariṁ vā manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṁ sacchikarissatīti ṭhānametaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: In the same way, that a mendicant whose mind is not clouded would know what’s for their own good, the good of another, or the good of both; or that they would realize any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones: this is quite possible.
Why is that?
Because their mind is unclouded.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yāni kānici rukkhajātānaṁ phandano tesaṁ aggamakkhāyati yadidaṁ mudutāya ceva kammaññatāya ca.
segs.e: “Just as, mendicants, the sandan is said to be the best kind of tree in terms of its pliability and workability,

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhikkhave, nāññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ bhāvitaṁ bahulīkataṁ mudu ca hoti kammaññañca yathayidaṁ cittaṁ.
segs.e: so too, I do not see a single thing that’s as pliable and workable as this mind that is developed and cultivated.

segs.p: Cittaṁ, bhikkhave, bhāvitaṁ bahulīkataṁ mudu ca hoti kammaññañca hotī”ti.
segs.e: A mind that is developed and cultivated is pliable and workable.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ lahuparivattaṁ yathayidaṁ cittaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that’s as quick to change as this mind.

segs.p: Yāvañcidaṁ, bhikkhave, upamāpi na sukarā yāva lahuparivattaṁ cittan”ti.
segs.e: So much so that it’s not easy to give a simile for how quickly the mind changes.”

segs.e: “Mendicants, those mendicants who explain an offense as an offense are acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Bahuñca te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū puññaṁ pasavanti, te cimaṁ saddhammaṁ ṭhapentī”ti.
segs.e: They brim with much merit and make the true teaching continue.”

segs.p: “Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū lahukaṁ āpattiṁ lahukā āpattīti dīpenti … garukaṁ āpattiṁ garukā āpattīti dīpenti … duṭṭhullaṁ āpattiṁ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpenti … aduṭṭhullaṁ āpattiṁ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpenti … sāvasesaṁ āpattiṁ sāvasesā āpattīti dīpenti … anavasesaṁ āpattiṁ anavasesā āpattīti dīpenti … sappaṭikammaṁ āpattiṁ sappaṭikammā āpattīti dīpenti … appaṭikammaṁ āpattiṁ appaṭikammā āpattīti dīpenti;
segs.e: “Those mendicants who explain a light offense as a light offense … a heavy offense as a heavy offense … a grave offense as a grave offense … a minor offense as a minor offense … a curable offense as a curable offense … an incurable offense as an incurable offense … an offense requiring amends as an offense requiring amends … an offense not requiring amends as an offense requiring amends

segs.p: te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bahujanahitāya paṭipannā bahujanasukhāya, bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: are acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Bahuñca te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū puññaṁ pasavanti, te cimaṁ saddhammaṁ ṭhapentī”ti.
segs.e: They brim with much merit and make the true teaching continue.”
Numbered Discourses 1.170–187
The Chapter on One Individual

segs.p: “Ekapuggalo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: “One individual, mendicants, arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
What one individual?
The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalo loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānan”ti.
segs.e: This is the one individual, mendicants, who arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”
“The appearance of one individual, mendicants, is rare in the world.
What one individual?
The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Imassa kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: This is the one individual, mendicants, whose appearance is rare in the world.”
“One individual, mendicants, arises in the world who is an incredible human being.
What one individual?
The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalo loke uppajjamāno uppajjati acchariyamanusso”ti.
segs.e: This is the one individual, mendicants, who arises in the world who is an incredible human being.”

segs.p: “Ekapuggalassa, bhikkhave, kālakiriyā bahuno janassa anutappā hoti.
segs.e: “The death of one individual, mendicants, is regretted by many people.
What one individual?
The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Imassa kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalassa kālakiriyā bahuno janassa anutappā hotī”ti.
segs.e: This is the one individual, mendicants, whose death is regretted by many people.”

segs.p: “Ekapuggalo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati adutiyo asahāyo appaṭimo appaṭisamo appaṭibhāgo appaṭipuggalo asamo asamasamo dvipadānaṁ aggo.
segs.e: “One individual, mendicants, arises in the world unique, without peer or rival, incomparable, matchless, unrivaled, unequaled, without equal, the best of men.
What one individual?
The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalo loke uppajjamāno uppajjati adutiyo asahāyo appaṭimo appaṭisamo appaṭibhāgo appaṭipuggalo asamo asamasamo dvipadānaṁ aggo”ti.
segs.e: This is the one individual, mendicants, who arises in the world unique, without peer or rival, incomparable, matchless, unrivaled, unequaled, without equal, the best of men.”

segs.p: “Ekapuggalassa, bhikkhave, pātubhāvā mahato cakkhussa pātubhāvo hoti, mahato ālokassa pātubhāvo hoti, mahato obhāsassa pātubhāvo hoti, channaṁ anuttariyānaṁ pātubhāvo hoti, catunnaṁ paṭisambhidānaṁ sacchikiriyā hoti, anekadhātupaṭivedho hoti, nānādhātupaṭivedho hoti, vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, arahattaphalasacchikiriyā hoti.
segs.e: “With the appearance of one individual, mendicants, there is the appearance of a great eye, a great light, a great radiance, and the six unsurpassable things; the realization of the four kinds of textual analysis; the penetration of many and diverse elements; the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom; the realization of the fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection.
What one individual?
The Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Imassa kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalassa pātubhāvā mahato cakkhussa pātubhāvo hoti, mahato ālokassa pātubhāvo hoti, mahato obhāsassa pātubhāvo hoti, channaṁ anuttariyānaṁ pātubhāvo hoti, catunnaṁ paṭisambhidānaṁ sacchikiriyā hoti, anekadhātupaṭivedho hoti, nānādhātupaṭivedho hoti, vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyā hoti, arahattaphalasacchikiriyā hotī”ti.
segs.e: This is the one individual whose appearance brings the appearance of a great eye, a great light, a great radiance, and the six unsurpassable things; the realization of the four kinds of textual analysis; the penetration of many and diverse elements; the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom; the realization of the fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekapuggalampi samanupassāmi yo evaṁ tathāgatena anuttaraṁ dhammacakkaṁ pavattitaṁ sammadeva anuppavatteti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, sāriputto.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single other individual who rightly keeps rolling the supreme Wheel of Dhamma that was rolled forth by the Realized One like Sāriputta.

segs.p: Sāriputto, bhikkhave, tathāgatena anuttaraṁ dhammacakkaṁ pavattitaṁ sammadeva anuppavattetī”ti.
segs.e: Sāriputta rightly keeps rolling the supreme Wheel of Dhamma that was rolled forth by the Realized One.”
Numbered Discourses 1.188–197
Chapter One

segs.p: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ rattaññūnaṁ yadidaṁ aññāsikoṇḍañño.
segs.e: “The foremost of my monk disciples in long standing is Koṇḍañña Who Understood.”
“… with great wisdom is Sāriputta.”
“… with psychic power is Mahāmoggallāna.”
“… who advocate austerities is Mahākassapa.”
“… with clairvoyance is Anuruddha.”
“… from eminent families is Bhaddiya son of Kāḷīgodhā.”
“… with a charming voice is Bhaddiya the Dwarf.”
“… with a lion’s roar is Bhāradvāja the Alms-Gatherer.”
“… who speak on the teaching is Puṇṇa son of Mantāṇī.”

segs.p: … saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ vibhajantānaṁ yadidaṁ mahākaccāno”ti.
segs.e: “… who explain in detail the meaning of a brief statement is Mahākaccāna.”
Numbered Discourses 1.198–208
Chapter Two

segs.p: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ abhinimminantānaṁ yadidaṁ cūḷapanthako.
segs.e: “The foremost of my monk disciples in creating a mind-made body is Cūḷapanthaka.”
“… who are skilled in the turning away of the mind is Cūḷapanthaka.”
“… who are skilled in the turning away through perception is Mahāpanthaka.”
“… who live without strife is Subhūti.”
“… who are worthy of a religious donation is Subhūti.”
“… who stay in the wilderness is Revata of the Acacia Wood.”
“… who practice absorption is Revata the Doubter.”
“… who are energetic is Soṇa Koḷivisa.”
“… who enunciate well is Soṇa of the Sharp Ears.”
“… who receive many possessions is Sīvali.”
“… who are committed to faith is Vakkalī.”
Numbered Discourses 1.209–218
Chapter Three

segs.p: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ sikkhākāmānaṁ yadidaṁ rāhulo.
segs.e: “The foremost of my monk disciples who want to train is Rāhula.”
“… who went forth out of faith is Raṭṭhapāla.”
“… who are the first to vote is Kuṇḍadhāna.”
“… who are eloquent poets is Vaṅgīsa.”
“… who are impressive all around is Upasena son of Vaṅgantā.”
“… who assign lodgings is Dabba the Mallian.”
“… who are beloved of the deities is Pilindavaccha.”
“… with swift insight is Bāhiya of the Bark Cloth.”
“… with brilliant speech is Kassapa the Prince.”
“… who have attained the methods of textual analysis is Mahākoṭṭhita.”
Numbered Discourses 1.219–234
Chapter Four

segs.p: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ bahussutānaṁ yadidaṁ ānando.
segs.e: “The foremost of my monk disciples who are very learned is Ānanda.”
“… in memory is Ānanda.”
“… in rememberance is Ānanda.”
“… in retention is Ānanda.”
“… as a personal attendant is Ānanda.”
“… with a large congregation is Kassapa of Uruvelā.”
“… who impress lay families is Kāḷudāyī.”
“… with good health is Bakkula.”
“… who recollect past lives is Sobhita.”
“… who have memorized the monastic law is Upāli.”
“… who advise the nuns is Nandaka.”
“… who guard the sense doors is Nanda.”
“… who advise the monks is Mahākappina.”
“… who are skilled in the fire element is Sāgata.”
“… who inspire eloquent teachings is Rādha.”
“… who wear coarse robes is Mogharāja.”
Numbered Discourses 1.235–247
Chapter Five

segs.p: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvikānaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ rattaññūnaṁ yadidaṁ mahāpajāpatigotamī.
segs.e: “The foremost of my nun disciples in long standing is Mahāpajāpati Gotamī.”
“… with great wisdom is Khemā.”
“… with psychic power is Uppalavaṇṇā.”
“… who have memorized the monastic law is Paṭācārā.”
“… who speak on the teaching is Dhammadinnā.”
“… who practice absorption is Nandā.”
“… who are energetic is Soṇā.”
“… with clairvoyance is Sakulā.”
“… with swift insight is Bhaddā of the Curly Hair.”
“… who recollect past lives is Bhaddā daughter of Kapila.”
“… who have attained great insight is Bhaddakaccānā.”
“… who wear coarse robes is Kisāgotamī.”
“… who are committed to faith is Sigālaka’s Mother.”
Numbered Discourses 1.248–257
Chapter Six

segs.p: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṁ upāsakānaṁ paṭhamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchantānaṁ yadidaṁ tapussabhallikā vāṇijā.
segs.e: “The foremost of my laymen disciples in first going for refuge are the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika.”
“… as a donor is the householder Sudatta Anāthapiṇḍika.”
“… who speak on the teaching is the householder Citta of Macchikāsaṇḍika.”

segs.p: … Catūhi saṅgahavatthūhi parisaṁ saṅgaṇhantānaṁ yadidaṁ hatthako āḷavako.
segs.e: “… who attract a congregation by the four ways of being inclusive is Hatthaka of Āḷavī.”
“… who donate fine things is Mahānāma the Sakyan.”
“… who donate nice things is the householder Ugga of Vesālī.”
“… who attend on the Saṅgha is the householder Uggata of Elephant Village.”
“… who have experiential confidence is Sūra Ambaṭṭha.”
“… who have confidence in an individual is Jīvaka Komārabhacca.”
“… who are trusting is the householder Nakula’s father.”
Numbered Discourses 1.258–267
Chapter Seven

segs.p: “Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, mama sāvikānaṁ upāsikānaṁ paṭhamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchantīnaṁ yadidaṁ sujātā seniyadhītā.
segs.e: “The foremost of my laywomen disciples in first going for refuge is Sujātā of the town of Senā.”
“… as a donor is Visākhā, Migāra’s mother.”
“… who are very learned is Khujjuttarā.”
“… who dwell in love is Sāmāvatī.”
“… who practice absorption is Uttarā, Nanda’s mother.”
“… who give fine things is Suppavāsā the Koliyan.”
“… who care for the sick is the laywoman Suppiyā.”
“… who have experiential confidence is Kātiyānī.”
“… who are trusting is the housewife Nakula’s mother.”
“… whose confidence is based on oral transmission is the laywoman Kāḷī of Kuraraghara.”
Numbered Discourses 1.268–277
Chapter One

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci saṅkhāraṁ niccato upagaccheyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to take any condition as permanent. That is not possible.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano kañci saṅkhāraṁ niccato upagaccheyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for an ordinary person to take some condition as permanent. That is possible.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci saṅkhāraṁ sukhato upagaccheyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to take any condition as pleasant.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano kañci saṅkhāraṁ sukhato upagaccheyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for an ordinary person to take some condition as pleasant.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci dhammaṁ attato upagaccheyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to take anything as self.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano kañci dhammaṁ attato upagaccheyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for an ordinary person to take something as self.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo mātaraṁ jīvitā voropeyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to murder their mother.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano mātaraṁ jīvitā voropeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for an ordinary person to murder their mother.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo pitaraṁ jīvitā voropeyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to murder their father.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano pitaraṁ jīvitā voropeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for an ordinary person to murder their father.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo arahantaṁ jīvitā voropeyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to murder a perfected one.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano arahantaṁ jīvitā voropeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for an ordinary person to murder a perfected one.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo tathāgatassa paduṭṭhacitto lohitaṁ uppādeyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to injure a Realized One with malicious intent.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano tathāgatassa paduṭṭhacitto lohitaṁ uppādeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for an ordinary person to injure a Realized One with malicious intent.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo saṅghaṁ bhindeyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to cause a schism in the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano saṅghaṁ bhindeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for an ordinary person to cause a schism in the Saṅgha.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo aññaṁ satthāraṁ uddiseyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for an individual accomplished in view to dedicate themselves to another teacher.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puthujjano aññaṁ satthāraṁ uddiseyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for an ordinary person to dedicate themselves to another teacher.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve arahanto sammāsambuddhā apubbaṁ acarimaṁ uppajjeyyuṁ. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for two perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas to arise in the same solar system at the same time.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ ekissā lokadhātuyā ekova arahaṁ sammāsambuddho uppajjeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for just one perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, to arise in one solar system.”
Numbered Discourses 1.278–286
Chapter Two

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve rājāno cakkavattī apubbaṁ acarimaṁ uppajjeyyuṁ. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for two wheel-turning monarchs to arise in the same solar system at the same time.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ ekissā lokadhātuyā eko rājā cakkavattī uppajjeyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for just one wheel-turning monarch to arise in one solar system.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ itthī arahaṁ assa sammāsambuddho. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a woman to be a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho, etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puriso arahaṁ assa sammāsambuddho. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for a man to be a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ itthī rājā assa cakkavattī. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a woman to be a wheel-turning monarch.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puriso rājā assa cakkavattī. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for a man to be a wheel-turning monarch.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ itthī sakkattaṁ kāreyya …pe… mārattaṁ kāreyya …pe… brahmattaṁ kāreyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a woman to perform the role of Sakka, Māra, or the Divinity.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ puriso sakkattaṁ kāreyya …pe… mārattaṁ kāreyya …pe… brahmattaṁ kāreyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for a man to perform the role of Sakka, Māra, or the Divinity.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ kāyaduccaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a likable, desirable, agreeable result to come from bad bodily conduct.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ kāyaduccaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for an unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable result to come from bad bodily conduct.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ vacīduccaritassa …pe… yaṁ manoduccaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: “It is impossible, mendicants, it cannot happen for a likable, desirable, agreeable result to come from bad verbal … bad mental conduct.

segs.p: Ṭhānañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṁ manoduccaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya. Ṭhānametaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: But it is possible for an unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable result to come from bad verbal … bad mental conduct.”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ kāyaduccaritasamaṅgī tannidānā tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjeyya. Netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.

segs.e: But it is possible that someone who has engaged in bad verbal … bad mental conduct could, for that reason alone, when their body breaks up, after death, be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

Numbered Discourses 1.296–305
Chapter One

segs.p: “Ekadhammo, bhikkhave, bhāvito bahulīkato ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: “One thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated, leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.
What one thing?
Recollection of the Buddha.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: This one thing, when developed and cultivated, leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.”

segs.p: “Ekadhammo, bhikkhave, bhāvito bahulīkato ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: “One thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated, leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.
What one thing?

segs.p: Dhammānussati …pe… saṅghānussati … sīlānussati … cāgānussati … devatānussati … ānāpānassati … maraṇassati … kāyagatāsati … upasamānussati.
segs.e: Recollection of the teaching. …” “Recollection of the Saṅgha. …” “Recollection of ethical conduct. …” “Recollection of generosity. …” “Recollection of the deities. …” “Mindfulness of breathing. …” “Mindfulness of death. …” “Mindfulness of the body. …” “Recollection of peace.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: This one thing, when developed and cultivated, leads solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.”
Numbered Discourses 1.306–315
Chapter Two

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannā vā akusalā dhammā uppajjanti uppannā vā akusalā dhammā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattanti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to unskillful qualities, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow like wrong view.

segs.p: Micchādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, anuppannā ceva akusalā dhammā uppajjanti uppannā ca akusalā dhammā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: When you have wrong view, unskillful qualities arise or, when they have arisen, they increase and grow.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannā vā kusalā dhammā uppajjanti uppannā vā kusalā dhammā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattanti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or, when they have arisen, makes them increase and grow like right view.

segs.p: Sammādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, anuppannā ceva kusalā dhammā uppajjanti uppannā ca kusalā dhammā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: When you have right view, unarisen skillful qualities arise or, when they have arisen, they increase and grow.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannā vā kusalā dhammā nuppajjanti uppannā vā kusalā dhammā parihāyanti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to unskillful qualities, or makes skillful qualities decline like wrong view.

segs.p: Micchādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, anuppannā ceva kusalā dhammā nuppajjanti uppannā ca kusalā dhammā parihāyantī”ti.
segs.e: When you have wrong view, unskillful qualities arise and skillful qualities decline.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannā vā akusalā dhammā nuppajjanti uppannā vā akusalā dhammā parihāyanti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to skillful qualities, or makes unskillful qualities decline like right view.

segs.p: Sammādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, anuppannā ceva akusalā dhammā nuppajjanti uppannā ca akusalā dhammā parihāyantī”ti.
segs.e: When you have right view, skillful qualities arise and unskillful qualities decline.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannā vā micchādiṭṭhi uppajjati uppannā vā micchādiṭṭhi pavaḍḍhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, ayonisomanasikāro.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to wrong view, and once arisen, makes it grow like irrational application of mind.

segs.p: Ayoniso, bhikkhave, manasi karoto anuppannā ceva micchādiṭṭhi uppajjati uppannā ca micchādiṭṭhi pavaḍḍhatī”ti.
segs.e: When you apply the mind irrationally, wrong view arises, and once arisen it grows.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannā vā sammādiṭṭhi uppajjati uppannā vā sammādiṭṭhi pavaḍḍhati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, yonisomanasikāro.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that gives rise to right view, or, once it has already arisen, makes it grow like rational application of mind.

segs.p: Yoniso, bhikkhave, manasi karoto anuppannā ceva sammādiṭṭhi uppajjati uppannā ca sammādiṭṭhi pavaḍḍhatī”ti.
segs.e: When you apply the mind rationally, right view arises, and once arisen it grows.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ uppajjanti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that causes sentient beings to be reborn, when their body breaks up, after death, in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell like wrong view.

segs.p: Micchādiṭṭhiyā, bhikkhave, samannāgatā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ uppajjantī”ti.
segs.e: It is because they have wrong view that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ uppajjanti yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that causes sentient beings to be reborn, when their body breaks up, after death, in a good place, a heavenly realm like right view.

segs.p: Sammādiṭṭhiyā, bhikkhave, samannāgatā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ uppajjantī”ti.
segs.e: It is because they have right view that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

segs.p: “Micchādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, purisapuggalassa yañceva kāyakammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yañca vacīkammaṁ …pe… yañca manokammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yā ca cetanā yā ca patthanā yo ca paṇidhi ye ca saṅkhārā sabbe te dhammā aniṭṭhāya akantāya amanāpāya ahitāya dukkhāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when an individual has wrong view, whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable, harmful, and suffering.
Why is that?
Because their view is bad.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, nimbabījaṁ vā kosātakibījaṁ vā tittakālābubījaṁ vā allāya pathaviyā nikkhittaṁ yañceva pathavirasaṁ upādiyati yañca āporasaṁ upādiyati sabbaṁ taṁ tittakattāya kaṭukattāya asātattāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: Suppose a seed of neem, angled gourd, or bitter gourd was planted in moist earth. Whatever nutrients it takes up from the earth and water would lead to its bitter, acerbic, and unpleasant taste.
Why is that?
Because the seed is bad.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhikassa purisapuggalassa yañceva kāyakammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yañca vacīkammaṁ …pe… yañca manokammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yā ca cetanā yā ca patthanā yo ca paṇidhi ye ca saṅkhārā sabbe te dhammā aniṭṭhāya akantāya amanāpāya ahitāya dukkhāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: In the same way, when an individual has wrong view, whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is unlikable, undesirable, disagreeable, harmful, and suffering.
Why is that?
Because their view is bad.”

segs.p: “Sammādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, purisapuggalassa yañceva kāyakammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yañca vacīkammaṁ …pe… yañca manokammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yā ca cetanā yā ca patthanā yo ca paṇidhi ye ca saṅkhārā sabbe te dhammā iṭṭhāya kantāya manāpāya hitāya sukhāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when an individual has right view, whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is likable, desirable, agreeable, beneficial, and pleasant.
Why is that?
Because their view is good.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ucchubījaṁ vā sālibījaṁ vā muddikābījaṁ vā allāya pathaviyā nikkhittaṁ yañceva pathavirasaṁ upādiyati yañca āporasaṁ upādiyati sabbaṁ taṁ madhurattāya sātattāya asecanakattāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: Suppose a seed of sugarcane, fine rice, or grape was planted in moist earth. Whatever nutrients it takes up from the earth and water would lead to its sweet, pleasant, delectable flavor.
Why is that?
Because the seed is good.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhikassa purisapuggalassa yañceva kāyakammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yañca vacīkammaṁ …pe… yañca manokammaṁ yathādiṭṭhi samattaṁ samādinnaṁ yā ca cetanā yā ca patthanā yo ca paṇidhi ye ca saṅkhārā sabbe te dhammā iṭṭhāya kantāya manāpāya hitāya sukhāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: In the same way, when an individual has right view, whatever bodily, verbal, or mental deeds they undertake in line with that view, their intentions, aims, wishes, and choices all lead to what is likable, desirable, agreeable, beneficial, and pleasant.
Why is that?
Because their view is good.”
Numbered Discourses 1.316–332
Chapter Three

segs.p: “Ekapuggalo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanaahitāya bahujanaasukhāya, bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: “One individual, mendicants, arises in the world for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.
What one individual?
Someone with wrong view, whose perspective is distorted.

segs.p: So bahujanaṁ saddhammā vuṭṭhāpetvā asaddhamme patiṭṭhāpeti.
segs.e: They draw many people away from the true teaching and establish them in false teachings.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalo loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanaahitāya bahujanaasukhāya, bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānan”ti.
segs.e: This is one individual who arises in the world for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.”

segs.p: “Ekapuggalo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya, bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: “One individual, mendicants, arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
What one individual?
Someone with right view, whose perspective is undistorted.

segs.p: So bahujanaṁ asaddhammā vuṭṭhāpetvā saddhamme patiṭṭhāpeti.
segs.e: They draw many people away from false teachings and establish them in the true teaching.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekapuggalo loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya, bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānan”ti.
segs.e: This is one individuals who arises in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ mahāsāvajjaṁ yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single thing that is so very blameworthy as wrong view.
Wrong view is the most blameworthy thing of all.”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekapuggalampi samanupassāmi yo evaṁ bahujanaahitāya paṭipanno bahujanaasukhāya, bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṁ yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, makkhali moghapuriso.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I do not see a single other individual who acts for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans, as that futile man, the bamboo-staffed ascetic.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, nadīmukhe khippaṁ uḍḍeyya bahūnaṁ macchānaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya anayāya byasanāya;
segs.e: Just as a trap set at the mouth of a river would bring harm, suffering, calamity, and disaster for many fish,

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, makkhali moghapuriso manussakhippaṁ maññe loke uppanno bahūnaṁ sattānaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya anayāya byasanāyā”ti.
segs.e: so too that futile man, the bamboo-staffed ascetic, is a trap for humans, it seems to me. He has arisen in the world for the harm, suffering, calamity, and disaster of many beings.”

segs.p: “Durakkhāte, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye yo ca samādapeti yañca samādapeti yo ca samādapito tathattāya paṭipajjati sabbe te bahuṁ apuññaṁ pasavanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the one who encourages someone in a poorly explained teaching and training, the one who they encourage, and the one who practices accordingly all brim with much wickedness.
Why is that?
Because the teaching is poorly explained.”

segs.p: “Svākkhāte, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye yo ca samādapeti yañca samādapeti yo ca samādapito tathattāya paṭipajjati sabbe te bahuṁ puññaṁ pasavanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the one who encourages someone in a well explained teaching and training, the one who they encourage, and the one who practices accordingly all brim with much merit.
Why is that?
Because the teaching is well explained.”

segs.p: “Durakkhāte, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye dāyakena mattā jānitabbā, no paṭiggāhakena.
segs.e: “Mendicants, in a poorly explained teaching and training, the donor should know moderation, not the recipient.
Why is that?
Because the teaching is poorly explained.”

segs.p: “Svākkhāte, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye paṭiggāhakena mattā jānitabbā, no dāyakena.
segs.e: “Mendicants, in a well explained teaching and training, the recipient should know moderation, not the donor.
Why is that?
Because the teaching is well explained.”

segs.p: “Durakkhāte, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye yo āraddhavīriyo so dukkhaṁ viharati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, in a poorly explained teaching and training an energetic person lives in suffering.
Why is that?
Because the teaching is poorly explained.”

segs.p: “Svākkhāte, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye yo kusīto so dukkhaṁ viharati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, in a well explained teaching and training a lazy person lives in suffering.
Why is that?
Because the teaching is well explained.”

segs.p: “Durakkhāte, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye yo kusīto so sukhaṁ viharati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, in a poorly explained teaching and training a lazy person lives happily.
Why is that?
Because the teaching is poorly explained.”

segs.p: “Svākkhāte, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye yo āraddhavīriyo so sukhaṁ viharati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, in a well explained teaching and training an energetic person lives happily.
Why is that?
Because the teaching is well explained.”
“Just as, mendicants, even a little bit of fecal matter still stinks,

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhikkhave, appamattakampi bhavaṁ na vaṇṇemi, antamaso accharāsaṅghātamattampi”.
segs.e: so too I don’t approve of even a little bit of continued existence, not even as long as a finger-snap.”

They develop the faculty of energy …
the faculty of mindfulness …
the faculty of immersion …
the faculty of wisdom …
the power of faith …
the power of energy …
the power of mindfulness …
the power of immersion …
the power of wisdom.
That mendicant is called

segs.p: ‘bhikkhu arittajjhāno viharati satthusāsanakaro ovādapatikaro, amoghaṁ raṭṭhapiṇḍaṁ bhuñjati’.
segs.e: a mendicant who does not lack absorption, who follows the Teacher’s instructions, who responds to advice, and who does not eat the country’s alms in vain.

segs.p: Ko pana vādo ye naṁ bahulīkarontī”ti.
segs.e: How much more so those who make much of it!”
Numbered Discourses 1.575–615
The Chapter on Mindfulness of the Body

segs.p: “Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo cetasā phuṭo antogadhā tassa kunnadiyo yā kāci samuddaṅgamā;
segs.e: “Mendicants, anyone who brings into their mind the great ocean includes all of the streams that run into it.

segs.p: evamevaṁ, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci kāyagatā sati bhāvitā bahulīkatā antogadhā tassa kusalā dhammā ye keci vijjābhāgiyā”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, anyone who has developed and cultivated mindfulness of the body includes all of the skillful qualities that play a part in realization.”

segs.p: “Ekadhammo, bhikkhave, bhāvito bahulīkato mahato saṁvegāya saṁvattati … mahato atthāya saṁvattati … mahato yogakkhemāya saṁvattati … satisampajaññāya saṁvattati … ñāṇadassanappaṭilābhāya saṁvattati … diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāya saṁvattati … vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: “One thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated leads to great urgency … great benefit … great sanctuary from the yoke … mindfulness and awareness … gaining knowledge and vision … blissful meditation in this life … the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.
What one thing?
Mindfulness of the body.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato mahato saṁvegāya saṁvattati … mahato atthāya saṁvattati … mahato yogakkhemāya saṁvattati … satisampajaññāya saṁvattati … ñāṇadassanappaṭilābhāya saṁvattati … diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāya saṁvattati … vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: This one thing, when developed and cultivated, leads to great urgency … great benefit … great sanctuary from the yoke … mindfulness and awareness … gaining knowledge and vision … blissful meditation in this life … the realization of the fruit of knowledge and freedom.”

segs.p: “Ekadhamme, bhikkhave, bhāvite bahulīkate kāyopi passambhati, cittampi passambhati, vitakkavicārāpi vūpasammanti, kevalāpi vijjābhāgiyā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchanti.
segs.e: “When one thing, mendicants, is developed and cultivated the body and mind become tranquil, thinking and considering settle down, and all of the qualities that play a part in realization are fully developed.
What one thing?
Mindfulness of the body.

segs.p: Imasmiṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekadhamme bhāvite bahulīkate kāyopi passambhati, cittampi passambhati, vitakkavicārāpi vūpasammanti, kevalāpi vijjābhāgiyā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchantī”ti.
segs.e: When this one thing is developed and cultivated, the body and mind become tranquil, thinking and considering settle down, and all of the qualities that play a part in realization are fully developed.”

segs.p: “Ekadhamme, bhikkhave, bhāvite bahulīkate anuppannā ceva akusalā dhammā nuppajjanti, uppannā ca akusalā dhammā pahīyanti.
segs.e: “When one thing, mendicants, is developed and cultivated, unskillful qualities do not arise, and, if they’ve already arisen, they are given up.
What one thing?
Mindfulness of the body.

segs.p: Imasmiṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekadhamme bhāvite bahulīkate anuppannā ceva akusalā dhammā nuppajjanti, uppannā ca akusalā dhammā pahīyantī”ti.
segs.e: When this one thing is developed and cultivated, unskillful qualities do not arise, and, if they’ve already arisen, they are given up.”

segs.p: “Ekadhamme, bhikkhave, bhāvite bahulīkate anuppannā ceva kusalā dhammā uppajjanti, uppannā ca kusalā dhammā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “When one thing, mendicants, is developed and cultivated, skillful qualities arise, and, once they’ve arisen, they increase and grow.
What one thing?
Mindfulness of the body.

segs.p: Imasmiṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekadhamme bhāvite bahulīkate anuppannā ceva kusalā dhammā uppajjanti, uppannā ca kusalā dhammā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: When this one thing is developed and cultivated, skillful qualities arise, and, once they’ve arisen, they increase and grow.”

segs.p: “Ekadhamme, bhikkhave, bhāvite bahulīkate avijjā pahīyati … vijjā uppajjati … asmimāno pahīyati … anusayā samugghātaṁ gacchanti … saṁyojanā pahīyanti.
segs.e: “When one thing, mendicants, is developed and cultivated, ignorance is given up … knowledge arises … the conceit ‘I am’ is given up … the underlying tendencies are uprooted … the fetters are given up.
What one thing?
Mindfulness of the body.

segs.p: Imasmiṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekadhamme bhāvite bahulīkate avijjā pahīyati … vijjā uppajjati … asmimāno pahīyati … anusayā samugghātaṁ gacchanti … saṁyojanā pahīyantī”ti.
segs.e: When this one thing is developed and cultivated, ignorance is given up … knowledge arises … the conceit ‘I am’ is given up … the underlying tendencies are uprooted … the fetters are given up.”

segs.p: “Ekadhammo, bhikkhave, bhāvito bahulīkato paññāpabhedāya saṁvattati … anupādāparinibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: “One thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated leads to demolition by wisdom … to complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping.
What one thing?
Mindfulness of the body.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato paññāpabhedāya saṁvattati … anupādāparinibbānāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: This one thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated leads to demolition by wisdom … to complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping.”

segs.p: “Ekadhamme, bhikkhave, bhāvite bahulīkate anekadhātupaṭivedho hoti … nānādhātupaṭivedho hoti … anekadhātupaṭisambhidā hoti.
segs.e: “When one thing is developed and cultivated there is the penetration of many elements … the penetration of diverse elements … the discrimination of many elements.
What one thing?
Mindfulness of the body.

segs.p: Imasmiṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekadhamme bhāvite bahulīkate anekadhātupaṭivedho hoti … nānādhātupaṭivedho hoti … anekadhātupaṭisambhidā hotī”ti.
segs.e: When this one thing is developed and cultivated there is the penetration of many elements … the penetration of diverse elements … the analysis of many elements.”

segs.p: “Ekadhammo, bhikkhave, bhāvito bahulīkato sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati … sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati … anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati … arahattaphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: “One thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated leads to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry … once-return … non-return … perfection.
What one thing?
Mindfulness of the body.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati … sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati … anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattati … arahattaphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: This one thing, when developed and cultivated, leads to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry … once-return … non-return … perfection.”

segs.p: “Ekadhammo, bhikkhave, bhāvito bahulīkato paññāpaṭilābhāya saṁvattati … paññāvuddhiyā saṁvattati … paññāvepullāya saṁvattati … mahāpaññatāya saṁvattati … puthupaññatāya saṁvattati … vipulapaññatāya saṁvattati … gambhīrapaññatāya saṁvattati … asāmantapaññatāya saṁvattati … bhūripaññatāya saṁvattati … paññābāhullāya saṁvattati … sīghapaññatāya saṁvattati … lahupaññatāya saṁvattati … hāsapaññatāya saṁvattati … javanapaññatāya saṁvattati … tikkhapaññatāya saṁvattati … nibbedhikapaññatāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: “One thing, mendicants, when developed and cultivated, leads to the getting of wisdom … the growth of wisdom … the increase of wisdom … to great wisdom … to widespread wisdom … to abundant wisdom … to deep wisdom … to extraordinary wisdom … to vast wisdom … to much wisdom … to fast wisdom … to light wisdom … to laughing wisdom … to swift wisdom … to sharp wisdom … to penetrating wisdom.
What one thing?
Mindfulness of the body.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato paññāpaṭilābhāya saṁvattati … paññāvuddhiyā saṁvattati … paññāvepullāya saṁvattati … mahāpaññatāya saṁvattati … puthupaññatāya saṁvattati … vipulapaññatāya saṁvattati … gambhīrapaññatāya saṁvattati … asāmantapaññatāya saṁvattati … bhūripaññatāya saṁvattati … paññābāhullāya saṁvattati … sīghapaññatāya saṁvattati … lahupaññatāya saṁvattati … hāsapaññatāya saṁvattati … javanapaññatāya saṁvattati … tikkhapaññatāya saṁvattati … nibbedhikapaññatāya saṁvattatī”ti.
segs.e: This one thing, when developed and cultivated, leads to the getting of wisdom … the growth of wisdom … the increase of wisdom … to great wisdom … to widespread wisdom … to abundant wisdom … to deep wisdom … to extraordinary wisdom … to vast wisdom … to much wisdom … to fast wisdom … to light wisdom … to laughing wisdom … to swift wisdom … to sharp wisdom … to penetrating wisdom.”
Numbered Discourses 1.616–627
The Chapter on Freedom From Death

segs.p: “Amataṁ te, bhikkhave, na paribhuñjanti ye kāyagatāsatiṁ na paribhuñjanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, those who don’t enjoy mindfulness of the body don’t enjoy freedom from death.

segs.p: Amataṁ te, bhikkhave, paribhuñjanti ye kāyagatāsatiṁ paribhuñjantī”ti.
segs.e: Those who enjoy mindfulness of the body enjoy freedom from death.”

segs.p: “Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, aparibhuttaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati aparibhuttā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, those who haven’t enjoyed mindfulness of the body haven’t enjoyed freedom from death.

segs.p: Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, paribhuttaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati paribhuttā”ti.
segs.e: Those who have enjoyed mindfulness of the body have enjoyed freedom from death.”

segs.p: “Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, parihīnaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati parihīnā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, those who have lost mindfulness of the body have lost freedom from death.

segs.p: Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, aparihīnaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati aparihīnā”ti.
segs.e: Those who haven’t lost mindfulness of the body haven’t lost freedom from death.”

segs.p: “Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, viraddhaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati viraddhā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, those who have missed out on mindfulness of the body have missed out on freedom from death.

segs.p: Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, āraddhaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati āraddhā”ti.
segs.e: Those who have undertaken mindfulness of the body have not missed out on freedom from death.”

segs.p: “Amataṁ te, bhikkhave, pamādiṁsu ye kāyagatāsatiṁ pamādiṁsu.
segs.e: “Mendicants, those who have neglected mindfulness of the body have neglected freedom from death.

segs.p: Amataṁ te, bhikkhave, na pamādiṁsu ye kāyagatāsatiṁ na pamādiṁsu”.
segs.e: Those who have not neglected mindfulness of the body have not neglected freedom from death.”

segs.p: “Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, pamuṭṭhaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati pamuṭṭhā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, those who have forgotten mindfulness of the body have forgotten freedom from death.

segs.p: Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, appamuṭṭhaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati appamuṭṭhā”ti.
segs.e: Those who haven’t forgotten mindfulness of the body haven’t forgotten freedom from death.”

segs.p: “Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, anāsevitaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati anāsevitā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, those who haven’t cultivated mindfulness of the body haven’t cultivated freedom from death.

segs.p: Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, āsevitaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati āsevitā”ti.
segs.e: Those who have cultivated mindfulness of the body have cultivated freedom from death.”

segs.p: “Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, abhāvitaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati abhāvitā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, those who haven’t developed mindfulness of the body haven’t developed freedom from death.

segs.p: Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, bhāvitaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati bhāvitā”ti.
segs.e: Those who have developed mindfulness of the body have developed freedom from death.”

segs.p: “Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, abahulīkataṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati abahulīkatā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, those who haven’t made much of mindfulness of the body haven’t made much of freedom from death.

segs.p: Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, bahulīkataṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati bahulīkatā”ti.
segs.e: Those who have made much of mindfulness of the body have made much of freedom from death.”

segs.p: “Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, anabhiññātaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati anabhiññātā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, those who haven’t had insight into mindfulness of the body haven’t had insight into freedom from death.

segs.p: Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, abhiññātaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati abhiññātā”ti.
segs.e: Those who have had insight into mindfulness of the body have had insight into freedom from death.”

segs.p: “Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, apariññātaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati apariññātā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, those who haven’t completely understood mindfulness of the body haven’t completely understood freedom from death.

segs.p: Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, pariññātaṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati pariññātā”ti.
segs.e: Those who have completely understood mindfulness of the body have completely understood freedom from death.”

segs.p: “Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, asacchikataṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati asacchikatā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, those who haven’t realized mindfulness of the body haven’t realized freedom from death.

segs.p: Amataṁ tesaṁ, bhikkhave, sacchikataṁ yesaṁ kāyagatāsati sacchikatā”ti.
segs.e: Those who have realized mindfulness of the body have realized freedom from death.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandunti.
segs.e: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.
The Book of the Ones is finished.
